architecture: Melting Point is a sustained DLC Orc steamtech/furnace talent and is not itself an event entry point. Its only caller is the Molten Metal passive's callbackOnTakeDamage, which the core damage pipeline invokes on the target for every non-instant? (every defaultProjector) hit whose damage type is not PHYSICAL or MIND. Trigger conditions: Furnace active, EFF_FURNACE_MOLTEN_POINT stacks >= 10, Melting Point sustained, steam > 15. On trigger, callTalent(T_MELTING_POINT, 'cleanActor') randomly removes up to floor(getTalentLevel) detrimental physical effects via removeEffectsFilter -> effectsFilter -> rng.tableSample -> dispel, drains 15 steam, force-uses Furnace Vent toward the damage source, and consumes the molten-point effect. Because cleanActor passes the actor itself as src, dispel forces allow_immunity=false, so the removal bypasses dispel resistance; effect type 'other' is still never touched by dispel without force. EFF_BURNING and EFF_BURNING_SHOCK are type='physical'/status='detrimental', so they lie in the random candidate pool and may be removed, but only if randomly sampled and only up to the count cap. No attribute, temporary value, timed effect, or callback grants any burn/burning/fire immunity at any point in the furnace tree: activate returns {}, deactivate returns true, and there are no ignore_fireburn/fire_immunity uses. Consequently existing burning may be cleared only as a side effect of the random physical-effect cleanse, and subsequent burning is applied normally (subject to the usual save/immunity checks). The real 'immune to fireburn' mechanic is a different class (Blacksmith Life in the Flames level 5), which sets the ignore_fireburn attr consumed by the DLC superload of on_set_temporary_effect to zero out EFF_BURNING/EFF_BURNING_SHOCK duration. Separately, Molten Metal reduces all non-physical/non-mind damage (including each FIRE burning tick, since FIRE is neither PHYSICAL nor MIND) by getResist * 0.75^stacks while Furnace is active; this is damage reduction, not immunity, and does not stop or prevent the burning effect.

There is an observed divergence between the Melting Point in-game description (which asserts a 'fire immunity serum' making the actor immune to the burning effect) and the code (which grants no immunity). This is reported as source evidence, not as a finding or verdict.

cleanActor's removal is random and capped (rng.tableSample with nb=floor(getTalentLevel)); BURNING/BURNING_SHOCK are only removed if sampled among other detrimental physical effects, so it is not a guaranteed burning cleanse.
Because removeEffectsFilter/dispel are invoked with src==self, allow_immunity is forced false, i.e. the cleanse ignores dispel resistance; but it still cannot touch effects of type 'other'.

Fire DOT effects are not all physical: the filter is type-based, so magical fire effects (e.g. BURNING_HEX, type magical) are not candidates while physical fire effects (BURNING, BURNING_SHOCK, BURNING_PHOSPHOROUS) are.

The only burning-immunity code found (ignore_fireburn) belongs to Blacksmith Life in the Flames, not to the furnace tree; Molten Metal's damage reduction is not immunity and does not prevent the effect.
